Shared damage caption grammar, reconstructed from both configured DF 53.16 PEs
===========================================================================

Source: data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. Static disassembly only; images are
not loaded or executed. reference-damage-status.asm and classic-damage-status.asm
were extracted again from these images. Native preferred base: 0x140000000.
Steam owner: 0x1400e56a0..0x1400e9f40, executable code ends at 0x1400e9e84.
Classic owner: 0x1400e5630..0x1400e9ed0, executable code ends at 0x1400e9e14.
For the shared constructor's instructions, Classic address = Steam - 0x70.
The source byte addresses and helper addresses are recorded separately in each
assembly listing; they must not be mapped using this constructor-only delta.

Complete text fields, not screenshot words
-----------------------------------------
actor [rbp+0xc0], actor-owner [rbp+0x120], actor-pronoun [rbp+0x140];
target [rbp+0xe0], target-owner [rbp+0x100], target-pronoun [rbp+0x160].
No projectile and no attacker: it / its / it (0x1400e579a..0x1400e57d5).
No projectile, attacker supplied: complete unit formatter 0x14132e430;
actor-owner is Your for adventure player, otherwise complete actor + 's;
actor-pronoun is You for adventure player, otherwise He/She/It from sex helper.
Projectile supplied: The + motion + COMPLETE item caption 0x140c65450;
actor-owner is its and actor-pronoun is It (0x1400e587d..0x1400e5951).
motion: flying when virtual +0x2a8 returns true or virtual item kind is 0x27
or 0x41; otherwise empty if projectile flags +0x48 & 0x480, else spinning.
These are all three native projectile actor alternatives, with their spaces:
  The flying {item}
  The spinning {item}
  The {item}
Target always comes from the complete unit formatter (0x1400e596e).
Target-owner is Your or complete target + 's; target-pronoun is You or He/She/It.
The unit formatter's appearance-bearing description, identity, profession,
species and RAW fields are complete dynamic fields. Splitting them into English
words loses ownership; a body adjective such as long-eyelashes is part of UNIT.

One head definition, reused by every main damage outcome
-------------------------------------------------------
The active attack record is selected by signed index context+0x4210 and stride
0xa8. Record strings are +0x20 prefix, +0x40 attack verb and +0x60 instrument;
flags are +0xa0, item target id +0x4, body target index +0x14.

if flags & 0x20:
    H = record.prefix;                 // COMPLETE caller-supplied prefix
else:
    relation = flags & 0x4 ? " by the " : " in the ";
    if flags & 0x8:
        object = complete item caption(item target id); // empty if not found
    else:
        object = complete body label(target, body target index, name index 0,
                                     number mode 2);
    direction = flags & 0x1 ? " from behind" :
                flags & 0x2 ? " from the side" : "";
    equipment = record.instrument.empty() ? "" : " with " + record.instrument;
    H = actor + " " + record.attack_verb + " " + target + relation + object +
        direction + equipment;

The head block is copied by the native source in each outcome. Representative
Steam block: 0x1400e5a31..0x1400e5b75; normal damage-list block:
0x1400e720b..0x1400e7343. The source proves optional direction and equipment
are independent and direction precedence is behind before side. No above/below
head alternative exists in this constructor. Attack verbs and instruments
are supplied complete by the record producer; they are not finite C strings
in this constructor. Generic RAW ATTACK_VERB values must use their typed scope.

Finite complete main-outcome sentence families
----------------------------------------------
  H + ", but it is deflected by " + DEFLECTION_OBJECT + "!"
  H + ", but the attack is deflected by " + DEFLECTION_OBJECT + "!"
  H + ", lightly tapping the target!"
  H + ", but there is no force!"
  H + ", but it passes right through!"
  H + ", but the attack passes right through!"
  H + ", but it glances away!"
  H + ", but the attack glances away!"
  H + " and the severed part sails off in an arc!"
  H + " and " + RESULT_LAYER + BODY_RESULT + "!"
  H + " and it is mostly cut away from the rest of the torso!"
  H + ", " + DAMAGE_LIST + "!"
  H + " and " + DAMAGE_LIST + "!"
  H + "!"

Deflection: flag 0x20 chooses it versus the attack. DEFLECTION_OBJECT is
target-owner + " " + COMPLETE item caption from a separate deflection record
selected by context+0x41ee (0x1400e5b94..0x1400e5c0e); if the item lookup fails,
the native builder appends only "!" without an object. This field is distinct
from the attack head's flag-0x8 item/body target choice.
BODY_RESULT finite suffixes, preserving their native leading spaces:
  " is smashed into the body, an unrecognizable mass"
  " splits in gore"
  " collapses"
  " is ripped into loose shreds"
  " is torn apart"
  " is cloven asunder"
  " explodes into gore"
  " collapses into a lump of gore"
  " is crushed"
RESULT_LAYER is the complete body/tissue/material field preceded by the, or
the native fallback the part / the injured part. Sources 0x1400e686d,
0x1400e6ac8 and the result suffix branches 0x1400e68b8..0x1400e6ccb.

Finite damage expressions and ordered combinations
--------------------------------------------------
LAYER is a complete body/tissue/material name, optionally BODY + "'s " + TISSUE.
LAYER_PHRASE = "the " + LAYER | "it".
VERB = tearing | tearing apart | shattering | chipping | fracturing | denting |
       bruising.
DAMAGE = VERB + " " + LAYER_PHRASE
       | "tearing it apart"
       | DAMAGE + " through a hole in the " + LAYER
       | "passing through a hole in the " + LAYER
       | "jamming the " + LAYER + " through the " + LAYER
       | "jamming the " + LAYER + " out of the wound"
       | "breaking away the " + LAYER
       | "breaking away" + FRACTION + " the " + LAYER.
FRACTION = " most of" | " half of" | " a piece of" | " the rest of".
Damage-selector branches: 0x1400e7605..0x1400e76c4; repeated layer selectors
0x1400e78d4..0x1400e79a5. Matching repeated damage verbs may be omitted, yielding
VERB + " the " + LAYER + " and the " + LAYER, preserving all layer fields.
DAMAGE_LIST is ordered DAMAGE joined with ", " or " and ", optionally followed
by " through the " + COMPLETE_EQUIPMENT and repeated " and spilling " + FLUID.
Equipment suffix source: 0x1400e82ff..0x1400e833f. Thus the screenshot's
bruising the muscle and bruising the heart through the large cow leather shirt
is one complete damage-list expression, with two separate tissue fields and
one complete equipment field. It is not three unrelated string replacements.

FLUID = OWNER + " " + [DECAY + " "] + MATERIAL.
DECAY = rancid | decomposing | rotten | fetid | foul | reeking | filthy |
        stinking. These alternatives occur at 0x1400e8418..0x1400e84a2.
An injection material can also be owner-free, using its complete RAW name.

Injury sentences: every native branch
------------------------------------
INJURY = ("a major artery" | "an artery") + [" in the " + BODY] +
             " has been opened by the attack"
       | ("many nerves" | "a motor nerve" | "a sensory nerve") +
             [" in the " + BODY] + (" have" | " has") + " been severed"
       | "a ligament" + [" in the " + BODY] + " has been " +
             (torn | sprained | bruised)
       | "a tendon" + [" in the " + BODY] + " has been " +
             (torn | strained | bruised).
Native injury flags: artery 0x40004000 (major bit14 precedes bit30), nerves
0xc00 (both -> many, bit10 -> motor, bit11 -> sensory), ligament 0x380
(bit9 torn before bit8 sprained before bit7 bruised), tendon 0x70
(bit6 torn before bit5 strained before bit4 bruised). many nerves uses have,
single nerves use has. Body suffix is omitted for the main injured body or
when the same body suffix has already been emitted within the injury list.
INJURY_LIST preserves order, joins with ", " / " and ", and appends "!".
All four native switch tables are decoded in native-switches.tsv, including
the three six-way record-kind 27..32 tables that accumulate these injury flags.

Auxiliary sentence families
---------------------------
The 29-way switch subtracts 6 from kind, bounds at 28, and dispatches kinds
6..34. native-dispatch.tsv and decompiled-productions.tsv retain each target.
  kind6: UNIT + (" have" | " has") + " been knocked unconscious!"
  kind7/8: UNIT + (" have" | " has") + " been stunned" + [" again"] + "!"
  kind9/10: UNIT + (" are" | " is") + " having " + ["more "] +
             "trouble breathing!"
  kind11/12: UNIT + (" feel" | " looks") + [" even more"] + " sick!"
  kind15: FLUID + " is injected into the " + OWNED_FLUID + "!"
  kind16: FLUID + (" pours over the " | " flows over the " |
             " splatters over the " | " crumbles over the ") + BODY + "!"
          state outside 0..3: FLUID + BODY + "!"; no verb or separator.
  kind17: FLUID + " is sucked out of the wound!"
  kind20: UNIT + (" are" | " is") + " propelled away by the force of the blow!"
  kind21: "The " + ITEM + " has lodged firmly in the wound!"
  kind22: UNIT + (" latch on firmly" | " latches on firmly") +
             " to " + OWNED_OBJECT + "!"
  kind23: UNIT + (" latch on firmly!" | " latches on firmly!")
  kind24: UNIT + (" have" | " has") + " become enraged!"
  kind34: OWNER + " attack is interrupted!"
  kind13/14/18/19/25/26/27/28/29/30/31/32/33: no auxiliary sentence.
Adventure player selects have/are/feel/latch, other subjects has/is/looks/latches.
UNIT is the complete target label or the native pronoun according to record
ownership flags, not an unrestricted substring. OWNED_FLUID in injection is
the complete target-owner + material field, not anatomy.

Additional non-switch sentences in this same owner
--------------------------------------------------
  "The geldables have been torn away!"
  "It is a gelding strike!"
  "It is a gelding blow!"
  EQUIPMENT + " is ripped to shreds!"
  EQUIPMENT + " breaks!"
All text-bearing branches, strings, inline operands, conditional jumps and
calls remain in the two assembly listings and native-literals/native-branches
source tables. These production families are a deduplication of native source
construction, not an observation or simulation of game rendering.

Explicit nullable-field control flow in the shared constructor
-------------------------------------------------------------
Only native conditional branches are included here. Arbitrarily empty or
malformed authored RAW strings are not expanded into speculative productions.
Classic shared-constructor instruction address = the Steam address below -0x70.

1. Attack-head item target: flags+0xa0 &0x8 selects lookup of item id+0x4;
   0x1400e5ae8 tests its result and branches to 0x1400e5b1c on null. The relation
   literal " in the " or " by the " was already appended. Therefore a head may
   end in " in the " / " by the ", or that empty target may precede the optional
   direction/equipment clauses. The shared attack scope has two exact no-object
   alternatives with source endings in the/by the, resolving the complete verb
   and unit but adding no absent body/item.

2. Separate deflection item: 0x1400e5bba branches directly to 0x1400e5c34 when
   lookup of the record at context+0x41ee fails. Native complete sentences are
   H + ", but it is deflected by !" and
   H + ", but the attack is deflected by !".
   The one space before ! belongs to the native suffix, not an empty capture.

3. A hole's target after normal damage: the literal " through a hole in the "
   is appended at 0x1400e7a9c. When its body differs from the two damaged bodies,
   0x1400e81d1 computes a complete body label but 0x1400e81f3..0x1400e8244 skips
   appending it if that body has at most one tissue. When a tissue should be
   appended, 0x1400e8282..0x1400e8285 explicitly skips a null tissue definition.
   Consequently the literal can be the complete final damage fragment, with no
   target, or it can retain BODY + "'s " with its tissue absent.

4. A hole's target before jamming: 0x1400e7c0f appends
   "passing through a hole in the ". For a different body, 0x1400e7c8b computes
   its body label but 0x1400e7cb4 branches to 0x1400e7d40 if tissue count<=1,
   again without appending that label. For multiple tissues, a non-main body
   gets BODY + "'s " at 0x1400e7cc8; 0x1400e7d2e..0x1400e7d31 can then skip
   a null tissue definition. 0x1400e7d40 always appends " and " and continues
   with the jamming expression. Thus these are not invented single-clause
   sentences: the empty hole production composes with the complete native
   following damage-list element, preserving that separate jamming action.

5. Breaking-away tissue lookup: the list separator is appended at 0x1400e7ff8
   or 0x1400e8001. 0x1400e807f..0x1400e8082 tests its tissue and on null jumps
   to 0x1400e82d5. That target ENDS the damage-record loop before optional
   equipment, fluid spill and ! suffixes; it does not process another record.
   Therefore only one final empty damage element is reachable. Native main
   sentences can be H + ", !" or H + " and !" when no earlier damage text was
   produced, or H plus a complete earlier damage-list and a dangling comma/and.
   There is no middle empty-list element followed by further damage and no
   repeated all-empty record list from this conditional branch. The grammar
   records only the two complete first-empty sentences and two trailing-list
   alternatives. The independent equipment suffix at 0x1400e82d9..0x1400e833f
   and fluid-spill loop at 0x1400e8351..0x1400e8527 still execute. Thus an empty
   first kind4 element can instead yield DAMAGE_LIST = "through the " + ITEM
   or "and spilling " + FLUID; both exact base alternatives compose with the
   ordinary subsequent spill/equipment productions. For an earlier complete
   list, its dangling separator stays part of the nonempty internal list span
   before the suffix. These translated consequences add no absent injury.

6. Fluid kind16 default state: 0x1400e9bc5..0x1400e9bda selects the four known
   state literals for 0..3. All other state values branch to 0x1400e9c07, which
   directly appends the complete body label and ! to the already-built fluid.
   FLUID + BODY + "!" is therefore an actual adjacent-field production, with
   no space and no flow predicate. Its rule resolves both fields in their
   existing fluid/body namespaces and supplies no absent verb.

Branches that do not produce an empty field
------------------------------------------
An empty instrument record is checked before adding " with ", so equipment is
simply omitted. Failed equipment lookup at 0x1400e82fd branches to 0x1400e8351
before " through the " is appended. A missing lodged-item record at
0x1400e9278 skips the entire auxiliary sentence. An invalid/unnamed body index
uses the body formatter's body part(s) fallback. Destructive body-result
tissue selection uses the part / the injured part fallback. These existing
productions already express the corresponding branches without epsilon rules.

Fluid material helper was also disassembled completely in both images:
  reference-material-caption.asm: 0x1414d1920..0x1414d1d79
  classic-material-caption.asm:   0x1414cc890..0x1414ccce9
For missing material lookup it appends the exact literal unknown material
(Steam 0x1414d1d44..0x1414d1d54; Classic 0x1414cccb4..0x1414cccc4), rather than
an empty string. Existing material and term translation namespaces cover this
literal. Valid RAW state names, owner names and virtual item captions remain
complete dynamic fields, not finite screenshot-specific substitutes.

Whitespace ownership required by these native branches
------------------------------------------------------
normalize_utterance folds doubled spaces but retains one native space before a
following comma, and, directional phrase or !. Recursive resolution trims a
complete internal semantic span, but the former suffix-fit and match gates
rejected such spans before resolution when their final byte was a space.
Only nonempty COMPLETE internal scopes head/attack/damage/damage-list/layer
need this trailing native-space admission for the conditional productions
above. Dynamic $unit/$item/$body/$term leaves retain their byte-edge rules;
no empty typed capture or unrestricted missing-field fallback is required.
